From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: André Klein <andre.klein@sonne-tech.com>, Lena Schmidt <lena.schmidt@greendalebank.de>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Mutual Action Plan — EU data localization & cross-border review: stakeholder onboarding

Hi André / Lena —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Per our conversation, I’m kicking off a short mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align on roles, timeline, and the evaluation checklist for the EU data-localization and cross-border review. Attached is a first-pass MAP draft and a short SLA overview to help surface any non-negotiables early.

High-level proposed timeline (flexible):
- Week 1 (Nov 28–Dec 4): stakeholder introductions, confirm technical/data owners, and kick off technical Q&A
- Week 2 (Dec 5–Dec 11): customer completes cross-border questionnaire and we provide follow-ups (DTIA/DPA inputs)
- Week 3–4 (Dec 12–Dec 25): technical evaluation and SOC/controls evidence review (note: reduced availability around holidays)
- Week 5–6 (Dec 26–Jan 8): legal alignment, contract redlines, and signoff; target commercial close by Jan 15, 2027

Primary asks to get started:
1) Please confirm the internal stakeholders who will own the data residency review (privacy/legal, procurement, and the technical owner).
2) Confirm whether Sonne needs a Data Processing Addendum (we can draft a DPA and DTIA inputs).
3) Book a 45-minute cross-border review with the combined team — proposed window Dec 3–4, mornings CET.

Attachments: 1) 2026-11-28_Redwood_MAP_EU_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet) 2) SLA-overview.pdf (summary)

I’ll loop in our technical and compliance leads below to keep things moving.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Laura —

Appreciate the clear plan. I’ve pulled in our DPO and procurement lead. Our initial list of contacts:
- Maria Alvarez (DPO) — maria.alvarez@sonne-tech.com
- Jonas Weber (Procurement) — jonas.weber@sonne-tech.com
- Lena (see cc) is coordinating privacy/legal from our bank partner side and will be on the call as well.

Quick notes:
- Yes, we will expect a DPA and a DTIA outline. If Redwood can send a draft DPA and any standard transfer mechanisms (SCCs / EU adequacy notes) that will speed legal review.
- Timeline looks reasonable. We have one internal compliance blackout Dec 20–26; if possible, we’d aim to complete tech evidence before that.

I’ll check availability for Dec 3–4 and come back with windows later today.

Thanks,
André

Adding our technical owners and a short checklist to make the first call productive:

- Solutions/PS lead: Marissa Cole — marissa_cole@redwood.com
- Compliance lead: Soojin Lee — soojin_lee@redwood.com

Suggested pre-call checklist (items we can provide ahead of the meeting):
- Short architecture diagram showing where customer data is processed and caches (1 slide)
- List of relevant controls evidence (SOC 2 snippets, encryption at-rest/in-transit statements)
- Draft DPA and proposed SCCs / transfer approach
- Example configuration for data residency pinning (how to pin to an EU region)

André — if Maria or Jonas have a preferred questionnaire template, we can ingest it directly into the MAP and return answers by Dec 7. Otherwise, we’ll share our standard cross-border questionnaire by end of day today.

Regards,
